one_liner: A project or program manager role at Virginia Tech (a state university), rank/level set by experience, based in Arlington or Blacksburg; duties not described.
fit_summary: With no description, fit is hard to judge. Daniel's consulting work at IEM on government emergency management and recovery projects could translate to project/program coordination, and Arlington is commutable from Manassas. Daniel's people and policy strengths help, but the actual focus (research, IT, outreach, etc.) is unknown and could make this a weak match.
eligibility: Open the full posting on Virginia Tech's careers site (jobs.vt.edu) to confirm duties, required qualifications and education. None are stated here.
"Open Rank" means the level (e.g., associate, senior) depends on experience. Check the minimum years of project management experience for each rank.
Confirm whether the role is based in Arlington or Blacksburg and whether you can choose. Blacksburg is about 4 hours from Manassas.
Check for any required degree or certification (e.g., PMP). Neither is stated in the facts provided.
strategy: Find the full announcement on Virginia Tech's site before applying; tailor your resume only after reading the real duties and minimum qualifications.
Frame your IEM experience around project work: government clients served, deliverables, deadlines, team coordination and client communication. Use your actual title and duties.
Emphasize relationship-building with government stakeholders and your policy knowledge, which suits university programs that interface with federal or state agencies (common at the Arlington campus).
State government/university resumes aren't held to the federal two-page rule, but keep yours to 1-2 pages focused on project outcomes.
Apply soon. "Open until filled" postings can close without notice once a strong pool exists.
Prepare a cover letter connecting your consulting background to the program's mission once known.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [number] [type] projects for [government client type] at IEM, managing schedules, deliverables and client communication to meet [deadline/requirement].
Served as liaison between [client agency/stakeholders] and project teams, facilitating [meetings/workshops] for [number] participants on [emergency management/recovery topic].
Tracked [budget/tasks/milestones] using [tool] and produced [weekly/monthly] status reports for [audience].
interview_questions: Describe a project you managed from start to finish. How did you handle scope, schedule and stakeholders?
How have you kept a project on track when priorities or client needs changed?
Tell us about a time you built a working relationship with a difficult stakeholder.
Why do you want to work in a university setting, and what interests you about this program?
watch_outs: No job description, salary or qualifications are provided. You must review the full posting before investing effort.
The Blacksburg location would require relocation or a very long commute from Manassas. Confirm that Arlington is an option.
Rank and pay depend on experience, and senior ranks may require years of formal PM experience or a PMP.
